text: NOAA CPC's discussion of 12 November 2026 keeps an El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January–March 2027 (a greater than 79% chance), and is expected to begin weakening in early 2027. The next discussion is scheduled for 10 December 2026.

Compared with the previous month, El Niño strengthened as sea surface temperature anomalies exceeded 4.0 °C and extended farther west across the eastern equatorial Pacific; the weekly Niño-3.4 index reached +2.5 °C, and suppressed rainfall persisted over Indonesia.

text: NOAA puts the chance of a historic event, with a 3-month RONI of +2.5 °C or more, at about 60% for October–December and November–January.
missing: noaa-disc: "~60% for the October-December and November-January periods"

text: NOAA verifies these probabilities with the Relative Oceanic Niño Index, defining El Niño and La Niña with ±0.5 °C thresholds in Niño-3.4 sea surface temperature departures from a 1991–2020 base period.

RONI is the three-month running mean of Niño 3.4 sea surface temperature anomalies with the average tropical anomaly subtracted, rescaled to the original index's variance; its latest values are estimates that can change for up to two months.

text: In Southeast Asia, El Niño typically brings drier-than-average rainfall, including for most of the Maritime Continent in September–November, raising the risk of forest fires and smoke haze; its effect is typically stronger over the southern and eastern parts of the region in June–October, and more pronounced in strong or moderate events.
